1/4 You can have the house, the stability, the relationships that look good on paper. Everything checks the boxes. And still wake up feeling like you're watching someone else live your life. That's not depression talking. That's misalignment.

2/4 The weird part? Your life might genuinely be working. You're not broken. Nothing catastrophic happened. But there's this subtle wrongness, like wearing clothes that fit perfectly but feel like they belong to someone else. You move through days that are objectively fine while something inside stays restless.

3/4 We're trained to fix the obvious problems. Bad job, bad relationship, bad health. We know the protocol. But what do you do when the problem isn't the life you have, it's that the life you have doesn't match who you're actually becoming? When your circumstances stayed the same but you didn't?

4/4 The emptiness isn't a sign of failure. Sometimes it's clarity wearing an uncomfortable jacket, telling you something deeper shifted. That the version of good you built no longer fits the person building it. Sitting with that, instead of scrambling to fill it, changes everything.
